arxiv-2005-10548.title: Coswara - A Database of Breathing, Cough, and Voice Sounds for COVID-19 Diagnosis
arxiv-2005-10548.description: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic presents global challenges transcending boundaries of country, race, religion, and economy. The current gold standard method for COVID-19 detection is the reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) testing. However, this method is expensive, time-consuming, and violates social distancing.

arxiv-2011-08230.title: Spectral Implications of Atomic Uncertainties in Optically-thin Hot Plasmas Journal: APJ
arxiv-2011-08230.creator: Keri Heuer, Adam R. Foster, Randall Smith
arxiv-2011-08230.description: Abstract Two new high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy missions, XRISM and Athena, will observe deeper and with higher X-ray resolution than ever before possible. Interpreting these new X-ray spectra will require understanding the impact that uncertainties on fundamental atomic quantities such as collisional cross sections, transition rates, and wavelengths have on spectral models.

arxiv-2012-04141.title: Extended Gini index
arxiv-2012-04141.creator: Ram Sewak Dubey, Giorgio Laguzzi
arxiv-2012-04141.description: Abstract We propose an extended version of Gini index defined on the set of infinite utility streams, X = Y ℕ X=Y^{\mathbb{N}} where Y ⊂ ℝ Y\subset\mathbb{R} . For Y Y containing at most finitely many elements, the index satisfies the generalized Pigou-Dalton transfer principles in addition to the anonymity axiom.

arxiv-2103-03374.creator: Ahmet Erdem Sarıyüce
arxiv-2103-03374.description: Abstract . Dense regions in networks are an indicator of interesting and unusual information. However, most existing methods only consider simple, undirected, unweighted networks. Complex networks in the real-world often have rich information though: edges are asymmetrical and nodes/edges have categorical and numerical attributes.

arxiv-2412-11129.title: Disentangling Coherent and Incoherent Effects in Superconductor Photoemission Spectra via Machine Learning
arxiv-2412-11129.creator: K. H. Bohachov, A. A. Kordyuk
arxiv-2412-11129.description: Abstract Disentangling coherent and incoherent effects in the photoemission spectra of strongly correlated materials is generally a challenging problem due to the involvement of numerous parameters. In this study, we employ machine learning techniques, specifically Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), to address the long-standing issue of the bilayer splitting in superconducting cuprates.

arxiv-2503-15867.title: TruthLens : Explainable DeepFake Detection for Face Manipulated and Fully Synthetic Data
arxiv-2503-15867.creator: Rohit Kundu, Athula Balachandran, Amit K. Roy-Chowdhury
arxiv-2503-15867.description: Abstract Detecting DeepFakes has become a crucial research area as the widespread use of AI image generators enables the effortless creation of face-manipulated and fully synthetic content, yet existing methods are often limited to binary classification (real vs. fake) and lack interpretability.

arxiv-2505-15371.title: Distributionally Robust Federated Learning with Client Drift Minimization
arxiv-2505-15371.creator: MOUNSSIF KROUKA, CHAOUKI BEN ISSAID, and MEHDI BENNIS (Fellow, IEEE)
arxiv-2505-15371.description: Abstract Federated learning (FL) faces critical challenges, particularly in heterogeneous environments where non-independent and identically distributed data across clients can lead to unfair and inefficient model performance. In this work, we introduce DRDM , a novel algorithm that addresses these issues by combining a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) framework with dynamic regularization to mitigate client drift.

arxiv-2511-11343.title: Global symmetries: locality, unitarity, and regularity
arxiv-2511-11343.creator: Ibrahima Bah, 1 Shlomo S. Razamat, 2 Michal Shemesh, 2 and Hannah Tillim 1
arxiv-2511-11343.description: Abstract We study the apparent tension between locality and unitarity for symmetries in quantum field theory. This emerges in the context of categorical symmetries where symmetry operators are generically non-invertible. We argue that locality imposes particular regularities in the action of symmetries on the Hilbert space.

pmc-11402969.title: Haplotype-based pangenomes reveal genetic variations and climate adaptations in moso bamboo populations
pmc-11402969.creator: Yinguang Hou, Junwei Gan, Zeyu Fan, Lei Sun, Vanika Garg, Yu Wang, Shanying Li, Pengfei Bao, Bingchen Cao, Rajeev K. Varshney, Hansheng Zhao
pmc-11402969.description: Moso bamboo (Phyllostachys edulis), an ecologically and economically important forest species in East Asia, plays vital roles in carbon sequestration and climate change mitigation. However, intensifying climate change threatens moso bamboo survival. Here we generate high-quality haplotype-based pangenome assemblies for 16 representative moso bamboo accessions and integrated these assemblies with 427 previously resequenced accessions.

pmc-12581528.title: Unraveling the mechanism of tetracycline-induced renal injury: an evaluation of drug safety based on network toxicology and molecular dynamics simulations
pmc-12581528.creator: Yimao Wu, Yalun Liang, Jintao Liang, Zifeng Chen, Bo Tang, Junlong Zhu, Yifeng Shen
pmc-12581528.description: BackgroundTetracyline, a widely used antibiotic, is associated with nephrotoxicity, though its underlying mechanisms require further investigation.MethodsWe investigated the toxicological process of tetracycline-induced renal injury using network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations. The potential targets of tetracycline were obtained by integrating target information from multiple databases, and a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was established.

pmc-13665643.description: BackgroundAnemia in pregnancy is a severe public health problem in low‐ and middle‐income countries, yet the uptake of recommended iron supplementation remains critically low.
